messages:
Diego M: FYI Polaris onboarding hit a weird pattern: their Python Cloud Functions (GCF) app is refreshing tokens on every cold start. We're seeing short bursts of refreshes -> 429s and then user-visible failures. Risk of renewal churn if this stays flaky.
Lina S: Do we have their logs? Cold starts -> parallel refreshes is a classic stampede.
Diego M: Pasted log extract they sent: 
```
2025-06-10T09:01:02Z coldstart init - refreshing token POST /v1/auth/refresh 201 id=tok_a1
2025-06-10T09:01:02Z coldstart init - refreshing token POST /v1/auth/refresh 201 id=tok_a2
2025-06-10T09:01:03Z request /v1/generate 429 error=rate_limit
2025-06-10T09:01:04Z coldstart init - refreshing token POST /v1/auth/refresh 429 error=rate_limit
```
Raj P: Looks like their function concurrency + short token TTL (~5m) + no cross-instance cache = N clients refreshing simultaneously. Are they on serverless plan?
Diego M: Yes, they run many lightweight functions across regions. They used default session TTL thinking SDK would auto-share tokens.
ops-bot: Rate-limits: window=60s, per_key_bucket=api:writes:minute, burst_quota=default-midtier
Lina S: Short-term mitigation for serverless: 1) Use a shared cache (Redis/MemoryStore) to store token per user/tenant, 2) Add singleflight/dedup on refresh so only one instance refreshes and others reuse promise, 3) Increase session TTL to 20m if acceptable.
Raj P: For Python GCF we can suggest this pattern (example):
```py
# singleflight refresh using an in-memory promise + fallback to redis
_refresh_lock = {}
async def get_token(key):
    if cache.exists(key):
        return cache.get(key)
    if key in _refresh_lock:
        return await _refresh_lock[key]
    async def _do_refresh():
        tok = await client.auth.refresh()
        cache.set(key, tok, ttl=18*60)
        return tok
    fut = asyncio.ensure_future(_do_refresh())
    _refresh_lock[key] = fut
    try:
        return await fut
    finally:
        _refresh_lock.pop(key, None)
```
Diego M: Also recommend exponential backoff + jitter on 429 and preventing sync refresh on init path (do it lazily on first API call).
Lina S: Operational options: offer temporary burst while they implement fix. We can do a 24-48h bump for them. Need support signoff.
support-team: Created ticket #SUP-10321 to review burst request and include logs. We'll run a manual quota bump pending engineering signoff.
Diego M: I'll send Polaris an action checklist: 1) implement token dedupe or Redis cache, 2) extend TTL if possible, 3) add jittered retry on 429, 4) run a 1-hour soak with 30 concurrent clients across regions and report 429 rate.
Raj P: Add guidance to avoid refreshing token in middleware during coldstart — do on-demand in request path and return a 503 to caller if token not available rather than retrying many times.
Diego M: I'll draft email with the code example and checklist. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
Lina S: If they want help pairing, offer a 2-hour enablement session.
Diego M: Will propose that in the email.
